title: Token-demand mirroring: HC alignment & tiered discount projection (FY28 Q1)
content:
Executive summary:

This workbook sketches a compact, review-ready view of how token demand trajectories ("mirror" patterns from a few large customers) interact with our headcount phasing and a proposed tiered-discount schedule. Purpose is to provide a short-run decision stub for Sales + Finance: which discount breakpoints we can afford at each incremental committed token band without violating margin targets, and what hires (eng / SRE / CS) are required to sustain defined SLOs under each demand scenario.

Key high-level conclusions (preliminary):
- Under a base case (monthly token growth of 8%), we can offer a shallow tiered discount up to 15% at the 3x volume band while keeping contribution margin >= 28% after allocating dedicated-capacity costs.
- Aggressive demand (+25% monthly) requires ~2.5 FTEs more in infra/SRE in Q1 to maintain latency targets (p50 < 60 ms for small-prompts), otherwise margin erosion from burst capacity will exceed discount savings.
- Conservative demand (-5% month) suggests delaying 3 hires (product + solutions eng) and replacing planned contract SRE capacity with spot burst credits to preserve runway.

Model assumptions (explicit):
- Reference period: FY28 Q1 (Jan–Mar 2027) forecasting window built from current FY27 run-rate.
- Token price base (hosted API): $0.0025 per 1k tokens for standard small-model baseline unit.
- Model mix buckets: small (S), medium (M), large (L). Relative cost per 1k tokens to Redwood (GPU/infra) = [S: $0.0009, M: $0.0016, L: $0.0038].
- Customer elasticity assumptions (used in sensitivity sweep): tier elasticity = 0.65 (demand uplift per pct discount), enterprise-negotiation delta = -0.15 (larger customers push deeper discounts than elasticity predicts).
- Headcount costs: loaded fully-burdened rates used: Eng = $220k/year, SRE = $240k/year, CS AE = $160k/year, Solutions Eng = $180k/year. Onboarding ramp: new hires ramp to 60% productivity in month 1, 80% in month 2, 100% in month 3.
- Capacity-cost mapping: incremental tokens -> mapped to GPU-hours using batch-efficiency curves (conservative binning used). Burst capacity priced at market spot + 30% premium.

Sheet layout / sections (how to read the workbook):
- Summary dashboard (top): volume bands, discount schedule, margin waterfall.
- Scenario tabs (Base, High, Low): token projections, cost of goods sold (COGS) breakdown, HC plan impact, bottom-line contribution margin.
- Sensitivity grid: discount % vs margin; break-even discount curves by model mix.
- HC phasing sheet: hire-by-week for critical functions with cost waterfall and burn delta.
- Ask / decision matrix: recommended price band triggers and required approvals.

Scenario detail (textual extract from sheets):
1) Base case (8% monthly growth):
- Start tokens (Jan): 12B tokens/month (mix S: 55%, M: 30%, L: 15%).
- Revenue (no discount): $30.0k equivalent at base price? (note: sheet shows full calc). Contribution margin (pre-discount, post-COGS, post-fixed infra): 32%.
- Recommended tiering: 0% (0-2x), 7% (2x-3x), 12% (3x-5x), >5x handled by dedicated capacity contract (separate P&L).
- Headcount: hire 1 SRE (start day 30), 1 infra infra-engineer (start day 45) to support increased KV-cache usage and autoscale rules.

2) High-demand (ad hoc +25% month over baseline):
- Immediate infra pressure: projected sustained GPU-hours increase 38% in month 1 of the spike.
- Financial impact: burst spend increases COGS by +9 p.p. if we don't commit to reserved capacity.
- Headcount: recommend immediate contractor SRE surge (6 weeks) + convert to 2 FTE SRE hires for Q1 to keep end-to-end latency SLAs.
- Pricing: deeper discounts materially increase lifetime value but require upfront investment; recommend a performance-linked credit (time-limited discount) rather than permanent price cut for first 3 months of surge.

3) Low-demand (-5% month):
- Save: defer hiring of 2 hires (solutions eng + product PM) for 8–12 weeks; renegotiate hiring cadence.
- Pricing: tighten experiment bands and push renewal discounts to later quarters.

Sensitivity analysis highlights (from the grid):
- Break-even discount for mixed model usage at 3x volume band: ~13.4% (if SRE hires are delayed).
- If large-model share increases by +10 p.p., break-even discount drops to ~8.1% (because L-model COGS dominates).
- Elasticity pulls: if customer elasticity >0.9, offering an additional 5% discount at 2x band can unlock >18% incremental demand, often justifying the short-term margin loss.

Operational triggers and guardrails (recommended):
- Trigger A (volume commit observed > 2.5x baseline sustained 30 days): open reserved-capacity negotiation; finance to escrow 30% of expected burst cost for first 90 days.
- Trigger B (Large-model share > 20% of a single account): require technical review (SRE + Applied ML) before approving discounts beyond 10% for that account.
- Trigger C (realized margin under 25% for two consecutive weeks): automatically pause discount escalations and review price protections.

Pro forma headcount plan (three-month snapshot):
- Jan: +1 SRE (H1 start), +0.5 AE (contract to hire), net hiring delta +1.5 FTE.
- Feb: +1 infra eng (H1 start), +1 solutions eng deferred depending on trajectory.
- Mar: decision point to hire 1 product manager if sustained growth >= 12% month-over-month.

Example micro-sensitivity table (text excerpt from the sheet):
- Column headings: Discount%, Volume uplift%, Incremental tokens, Additional COGS ($), Additional HC cost ($), Net contribution delta ($), Margin after change (%)
- Row sample: 5%, +3.2%, +0.38B, +$9.6k, +$0, +$4.3k, 30.7%

Open questions and items for cross-team review:
- Sales request (thread in Slack): two customers asking for a 22% committed band at 4x. Need legal + finance pre-approval: can we cap discount by runtime SLA? (see linked Slack thread).
- Applied ML: confirm model mix shift probability if we activate quantized-medium as default; sheet contains an alternate cost ladder for quantized runs (reduces L cost by ~18%).
- SRE: confirm realistic onboarding ramp assumptions for contractors vs FTEs (sheet uses conservative FTE ramp).

Requests / next steps for this review cycle:
1) Finance: sanity-check the loaded HC rates and confirm whether any planned compensation bands will change before Jan hiring window.
2) Sales leadership: provide a short list (top 8 accounts) that might trigger the >3x band so we can pre-negotiate SLA and capacity commitments.
3) Product/Applied ML: supply the quantization adoption plan and probability for FY28 so the model-mix sensitivity can be reweighted.
4) Exec: decision on whether to permit time-limited promotional credits vs permanent discounting for first-movers.

Appendix (sheet notes):
- All monetary values are USD.
- The workbook includes a Monte Carlo shock simulation (1000 draws) for spot-price volatility on burst GPU and for customer churn; results live on the Sensitivity tab.
- Link to the working scenario sheet (internal): CONFLUENCE:FIN-Token-Demand-Model-2026.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally compact and uses conservative COGS assumptions; if you want a more aggressive growth story, switch the elasticity vector in the Sensitivity tab and re-run the breaker script (tab "run-sens").
- I flagged two accounts with large-model heavy usage — folks in Applied ML should check whether quantization can be offered as a negotiated term instead of lower $/token.
